sources.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, pre-publication version 2025-10-21
sources.reading_verification: Full 852-page author-hosted PDF fetched (HTTP 200, 9,643,655 bytes, SHA-256 d07177aa0317c13490c170fc6ccc6a2ee07989a9120d9958ed3453eefe5b2784) and the bodies of §§20.1-20.2, 18.4, 16.2 and 22.4.10/22.4.13 were read in the extracted text; the same file is the repository's audited V25 lane (research/algebraic-geometry-expansion-2026-09-30/source-vakil.md).

contents.name: Definition 20.1.1 (intersection product as signed sum of Euler characteristics; warning dim Supp F <= n)
Exercise 20.1.A (L = O_X makes the product vanish)
Exercise 20.1.B (invariance of the product under field extension)
contents.reason: Vakil20.1.B compares the pairing before and after extension of the ground field. All four local surface Statements quantify over an arbitrary FIXED field and their actual proofs calculate over that field; no comparison between two fields is asserted or needed.

contents.name: Exercise 20.1.C(a) (a line bundle on a projective curve has (L . X) = deg L)
Exercise 20.1.C(b) (recovery of Bezout for hypersurfaces)
contents.reason: Vakil20.1.C(b) recovers plane Bezout. The binding AG-SURF-1 design explicitly forbids repeating AV8 plane Bezout; ex-intersection-pairing-on-p2 proves numerical de without claiming to re-prove the local intersection-length sum theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 20.1.D (intersection with an effective Cartier divisor restricts to the divisor)
Definition 20.1.2 (writing an effective Cartier divisor in place of O(D)) and Remark 20.1.4 (additive notation)
Proposition 20.1.3 with proof §20.1.5 (symmetry and multilinearity of the product for projective X)
Exercise 20.1.E (base case n = 1 of the induction, by degree additivity on curves)
Exercises 20.1.F and 20.1.G (the defect rewritten as an (n+1)-fold product; vanishing when a factor is O(D) with D avoiding the associated points)
Exercise 20.1.H (an (n+1)-fold product with support dimension < n+1 vanishes)
Proposition 20.1.6 (dependence only on numerical equivalence)
contents.reason: Vakil20.1.6 compares numerically equivalent line bundles. Numerical equivalence itself is not introduced on the frozen pair; the exact Definition proves only isomorphism/linear-equivalence invariance, sufficient for all subsequent calculations.

contents.name: Exercise 20.1.I (asymptotic Riemann-Roch; the leading coefficient is an intersection number)
contents.reason: Vakil20.1.I identifies the asymptotic coefficient with an intersection number. The local four-term Euler formula is exact for fixed bundles; no proof requires asymptotic Riemann–Roch or a leading-coefficient interpretation.

contents.name: Exercise 20.1.J and Remark 20.1.8 (projection formula for a morphism)
Exercise 20.1.K (positivity of the product with ample line bundles)
contents.reason: Vakil20.1.K is positivity against ample classes. The AG-SURF-1 design does not promise positivity or Nakai–Moishezon; its local proof expresses line bundles as differences of effective divisors using global generation and requires no sign theorem.

contents.name: §20.2 introduction and Exercise/Definition 20.2.A(a) (the four descriptions of C . D and degree of the restriction)
Exercise 20.2.A(b) (length of the scheme-theoretic intersection when C avoids the associated points of D)
contents.reason: Vakil20.2.A(b) is the finite scheme-intersection LENGTH interpretation under avoidance of associated points. The frozen four A claims commission restriction DEGREE and point-blowup calculus, not general surface length equality. thm-intersection-with-curve-as-degree-of-restriction proves the promised identity by its two exact twisting sequences even when divisors share components; no finite-intersection length assertion is silently used.

contents.name: Remarks 20.2.1-20.2.3 (associated points of divisors, negativity, and the normal bundle as self-intersection)
Exercise 20.2.B (adjunction and Riemann-Roch for surfaces)
contents.reason: The actual planned destination surface-riemann-roch-and-the-hodge-index-theorem at897 commissions surface RR, Hodge index and primitive negativity. It is NOT one of the selected30pairs, contrary to the old reason. The present intersection proofs close without it; this is a genuine later planned deferral, not a promised selected supplier or forward dependency.

contents.name: Exercise 20.2.C (the intersection form of P^1 x P^1)
contents.reason: Owner design AG-SURF-1 B inventory at expansion-track row252 explicitly lists P2, BlP2 and the Cartier/complementary-dimension counterexample. The separate P1xP1 computation in Vakil20.2.C is neither commissioned there nor used by the actual two examples.

contents.name: Exercise 20.2.D with Hint 20.2.7 and Exercise 20.2.E (blown-up projective plane: l.l = 1, e.e = -1, l.e = 0)
Remark 20.2.8 (definition of a (-1)-curve)
§20.2.9 (the self-intersection of a fibre of a fibration is zero)
contents.reason: Vakil20.2.9 computes the square of a fiber of a fibration. The commissioned BlP2 class l−E does have square zero, but its proof expands a fixed class using the point-blowup matrix and does not assert or need a general fibration theorem.

contents.name: Exercise 18.4.L (Riemann-Roch for nonreduced curves: the Euler-characteristic shift by degree)
Exercise 18.4.M (degree is additive on a projective, equivalently proper, curve)
Exercises 16.2.F and 16.2.K (writing a line bundle as a difference of very ample divisors avoiding prescribed points)
Exercise 18.6.A (a very ample section can be chosen nonvanishing at the associated points)
contents.reason: Vakil18.6.A chooses a section avoiding all associated points on a general scheme. Surface bilinearity Proof1.2 needs only one nonzero section on integral X: its local rings are domains and its unique associated generic point is avoided by nonzeroness. F5 uses the actual earlier global-section-effective-divisor supplier, not the general avoidance exercise.

contents.name: §22.4.13 with Exercise 22.4.O (blowups and line bundles; O_X(E)|_E = O_E(-1))
§22.4.10 (blowing up an effective Weil divisor that is not Cartier)

sources.title: The Stacks Project, Varieties, Section 33.44 (Degrees on curves)
sources.reading_verification: Complete section page fetched (HTTP 200) and the full text read, including the proofs of Lemmas 33.44.3-33.44.7 and 33.44.9; used through the published local suppliers def-degree-invertible-sheaf-proper-dimension-one and the devissage chain.

contents.name: Definition 33.44.1 (tag 0AYR): deg(L) = chi(X,L) - chi(X,O_X) for an invertible module on a proper scheme of dimension <= 1
Lemma 33.44.2 (tag 0B59): degree is unchanged by field extension
contents.reason: Stacks33.44.2 compares bundle degree under field extension using flat cohomology base change. Current degree Definition and curve additivity quantify over each field separately; the actual surface proof never substitutes that comparison.

contents.name: Lemma 33.44.3 (tag 0AYS): degree is additive in short exact sequences of finite locally free modules
Lemma 33.44.4 (tag 0AYU): degree is invariant under birational morphisms of proper curves
contents.reason: Stacks33.44.4 proves degree invariance under birational morphisms of proper curves, including a more general generic-component correspondence. The surface point pullback calculation instead uses the actual acyclic direct-image comparison and projection formula on surfaces, and never invokes this general curve-degree invariance.

contents.name: Lemma 33.44.5 (tag 0AYV): chi(X, E (x) F) = r deg(E) + n chi(X,F) on a proper curve
Lemma 33.44.6 (tag 0AYW): degree decomposes over irreducible components with multiplicities
contents.reason: Stacks33.44.6 is the generic-component multiplicity expression for bundle degrees. The local cor-degree-additive-proper-curve Proof2.1–3.1 establishes its three numerical identities on the whole possibly nonreduced curve by devissage; no component decomposition is an input or an advertised output.

contents.name: Lemma 33.44.7 (tag 0AYX): deg(E (x) V) = rank(E) deg(V) + rank(V) deg(E)
Lemma 33.44.9 (tag 0AYY): an effective Cartier divisor on a proper curve is finite of degree dim_k Gamma(D,O_D)
Lemmas 33.44.10-33.44.15 (divisibility of degrees, positivity, and ampleness and section criteria on curves)
contents.reason: Stacks33.44.10–15 give divisibility, degrees of nonconstant maps, positivity/sections and ampleness characterizations. The actual surface proof uses earlier eventual global generation, then curve tensor-degree additivity; none of these additional degree criteria is a supplier, and no claim that all are already published in this run is needed.

sources.title: The Stacks Project, Varieties, Section 33.45 (Numerical intersections)
sources.reading_verification: Complete section page fetched (HTTP 200) and the full text read, including the proofs of Lemma 33.45.1, Lemma 33.45.5, Lemma 33.45.8 and Lemma 33.45.12; the coefficient definition and the alternating-sum comparison for d = 2 are the second independent treatment of the surface pairing.

contents.name: Lemma 33.45.1 (tag 0BEM): chi(X, F (x) L_1^{n_1} (x) ... ) is a numerical polynomial of total degree <= dim Supp F
contents.reason: Stacks33.45.1 proves a numerical polynomial for arbitrary coherent sheaves on arbitrary proper schemes. Surface bilinearity Proof1.1 uses the curve quadratic identity and Cartier twisting sequences, then differences of effective divisors. That route proves every commissioned surface identity without the broader polynomial theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 33.45.2 (tag 0BEN): the leading coefficient depends on lengths at generic points
contents.reason: Stacks33.45.2 identifies the leading numerical-polynomial coefficient through generic lengths. No local definition or proof extracts a leading coefficient: the intersection is an exact four-term Euler difference and its bilinearity is proved by the curve defect identity.

contents.name: Definition 33.45.3 (tag 0BEP): the intersection number as the coefficient of n_1...n_d
Lemma 33.45.4 (tag 0BEQ): the intersection number is an integer
Lemma 33.45.5 (tag 0BER): additivity of the intersection number
Lemma 33.45.6 (tag 0BES): additivity over irreducible components with multiplicities
contents.reason: Stacks33.45.6 decomposes numerical intersections into top-dimensional component multiplicities. Nonreduced Cartier curves ARE permitted locally, contrary to the old reason, but cor-degree-additive-proper-curve Proof1.2–3.1 treats them by coherent devissage directly. Neither a component-weighted cycle pairing nor numerical-polynomial coefficients are commissioned.

contents.name: Lemma 33.45.7 (tag 0BET): the pullback formula for a morphism of proper schemes
Lemma 33.45.8 (tag 0BEU): reduction of (L_1 ... L_d . Z) to an effective Cartier divisor
Lemma 33.45.9 (tag 0BEV) and Definition 33.45.10 (tag 0BEW): positivity and degree with respect to an ample bundle
contents.reason: Stacks33.45.9–10 develop ample positivity and polarized degrees of arbitrary closed subschemes. The frozen AG-SURF-1 inventory promises bilinearity, restriction degree and point-blowup matrix only; explicit P2 and BlP2 examples use Euler polynomials, not ample positivity.

contents.name: Lemma 33.45.12 (tag 0BEY): (L . Z) = deg(L|_Z) for a closed subscheme of dimension <= 1
Proposition 33.45.13 (tag 0BJ8): asymptotic Riemann-Roch
contents.reason: Stacks33.45.13 is the leading asymptotic section-count term for an ample bundle on arbitrary proper schemes. Local surface bilinearity uses eventual global GENERATION only, not section-count asymptotics; no local Statement identifies a Hilbert coefficient.

sources.locator: Section 31.33, tags 01OF-0806 and 02OS, read in full; the blowup construction itself is scaffolded on the batch-2 page blowups-exceptional-divisors-and-strict-transforms
sources.reading_verification: Complete section page fetched (HTTP 200, 42,047 bytes) and read; in particular Lemma 31.33.4 (tag 02OS) was inspected: b is an isomorphism off Z, E = b^{-1}(Z) is an effective Cartier divisor, and O_{X'}(-1) = O_{X'}(E), which is the sign convention used by lem-blowup-intersection-matrix-at-smooth-point.

contents.name: Definition 31.33.1 (tag 01OF): the blowup b: X' -> X of a closed subscheme, with twists O_{X'}(n)
contents.reason: The selected batch2 def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal constructs relative Rees Proj, its twists and local charts. Batch26 consumes that exact earlier supplier; its duplicate source row may defer there without building a second blowup definition.

contents.name: Lemma 31.33.3 (tag 0805): flat base change of blowups
contents.reason: The selected batch2 theorem thm-blowup-base-change-flat proves the exact flat Rees/tensor comparison, and its corrected companion supplies the nonflat failure. Batch26 already requires that page; retaining this duplicate row as a deferral to the actual selected supplier is sound and introduces no later premise.

contents.name: Lemma 31.33.4 (tag 02OS): isomorphism off the center, E effective Cartier, O_{X'}(-1) = O_{X'}(E)
